A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page versions of OVSeg3R. Their main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures and Appendices A.1-A.3 support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments in Tables 1-2, ablations in Tables 3-4, and qualitative predictions in Figures 4-7, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations and qualitative predictions in Tables 1-4 and Figures 4-7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.2 retain the same OVSeg3R training procedure, SegDINO3D-VL model, View-wise Instance Partition, boundary-aware superpoints and superpoint construction algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use ScanNetv2, ScanNet200, their MASt3R-SLAM/VGGT reconstructions, and the same in-the-wild examples in Section 5 and Appendix A.3. No dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in both benchmark tables. For example, Table 2 retains PLA, OpenScene+Mask3D, OpenMask3D, Open3DIS and Any3DIS (SAM2-L), with no additions or removals.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 retain the same 1,201-training/312-evaluation scene split, open and standard settings, base/novel class definitions, training-data combinations and mAP metrics. The ablation configurations also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 3-4 retain the same VIP/IBSp, reconstruction-data quantity/source, reconstruction-quality and input-feature ablations. Figures 4-7 preserve the same qualitative cases, including all appendix examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. OVSeg3R retains 40.7 overall mAP in Table 1 and 24.6 overall/24.2 novel-class mAP in Table 2; Tables 3-4 and Figures 4-7 also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(6), mathematical definitions, stated assumptions and the formulation in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. No theorem, proof or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about learning open-vocabulary 3D segmentation from 2D models, stabilizing training and improving category generalization.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of training stability and category-generalization gains, the qualification that VIP lacks guaranteed correct view assignment in Section 3.2, and the reconstruction-quality discussion in Appendix A.1.

D1.justification: Implementation information in Section 4.3 and algorithmic details in Appendix A.2 are identical. No hyperparameter, hardware, training-time or code/data-access information changes; the new funding acknowledgement adds no technical reproducibility detail.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the paper's positioning relative to prior research are unchanged. Bibliography entries move between pages without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 7, acknowledging partial support from Meituan Academy of Robotics Shenzhen, and corrects a missing period in the introduction. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the scientific prose and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement shifts the references downward on page 10 and reflows bibliography entries across pages 10-13. Figures 1-7, Tables 1-4 and all appendix pages retain identical displays and layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and a punctuation correction, with accompanying bibliography reflow. The methods, evidence, interpretations and appendices are unchanged. These limited editorial and administrative updates do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
